sentences.text: The genus Ptychotherates contains only one known species, Ptychotherates bucculentus, which is known from a nearly complete but somewhat disarticulated partial skull.
This dinosaur possesses a jugal bone that is unusually tall and deeper than in any other known Triassic dinosaur, a feature reflected in its specific name meaning 'with full cheeks'.
The generic name Ptychotherates is derived from Greek words meaning 'fold' and 'hunter'.

The fossil material of Ptychotherates was discovered in 1982 at the Coelophysis Quarry in Ghost Ranch, New Mexico, and the holotype specimen is now housed at the Carnegie Museum of Natural History in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.

Ptychotherates shares distinctive features with Tawa hallae, including specific bone fossae and a dorsoventrally tall, laterally flat jugal, distinguishing it from other coeval ornithodirans by having the proportionally deepest jugal known for any Triassic-aged dinosaur.
Ptychotherates is classified as a saurischian dinosaur belonging to the novel clade Morphoraptora, where it is closely related to Chindesaurus, Daemonosaurus, and Tawa within the group Herrerasauria.

Ptychotherates lived during the Late Triassic, specifically the Norian or Rhaetian ages, at the Chinle Formation at Ghost Ranch, New Mexico, United States, with a time range estimated between 205.7 and 201.4 million years ago.
